package_info.why_malicious: These versions of the package were compromised in a supply chain attack. Malicious code was injected to hijack cryptocurrency transactions by silently redirecting user funds to attacker-controlled wallets via a rogue WalletConnect project, resulting in direct theft of assets.

execution_context.trigger: runtime, upon WalletConnect session initialization and transaction request handling
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript bundle of @ledgerhq/connect-kit (index.js or equivalent entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initializes a WalletConnect instance with an attacker-controlled project ID, intercepts transaction requests, replaces the recipient address in 'eth_sendTransaction' calls with a hardcoded attacker wallet address, and forwards the modified transaction, resulting in silent redirection of user funds to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts and modifies outgoing cryptocurrency transaction requests, replacing the intended recipient with a hardcoded attacker-controlled address. This manipulation is performed without user knowledge or consent, directly enabling theft of funds.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate wallet connection library should securely relay user-authorized transactions without altering transaction parameters. Modifying the recipient address in a transaction, especially without explicit user approval, is a severe violation of expected security and trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate WalletConnect integrations may process and forward user-approved transactions, but they never alter transaction parameters such as the recipient address without explicit user action and confirmation.
key_indicators: Initialization of WalletConnect with a non-official, attacker-controlled project ID
Presence of a hardcoded cryptocurrency wallet address (e.g., 0x658729879fca881d9526480b82ae00efc54b5c2d) in the code
Interception and modification of 'eth_sendTransaction' parameters at runtime
No user notification or consent when transaction recipient is changed
Modification occurs in the main entry file (index.js) of the package

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Ledger's npmjs.com account credentials via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to upload and publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit to the npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all downstream applications and users installing these versions

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in applications using the compromised package, hijacking WalletConnect sessions and monitoring for transaction requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: User-initiated transactions are intercepted and transaction parameters are modified

attack_chain.action: Transaction recipient addresses are replaced with the attacker's wallet address, resulting in unauthorized redirection of funds.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen cryptocurrency directly into their wallet

behavioral_signatures: WalletConnect initialization using unknown or non-official project IDs
Interception and modification of transaction parameters, specifically 'eth_sendTransaction', at runtime
Presence of hardcoded cryptocurrency wallet addresses in JavaScript source code
Silent redirection of transaction recipient addresses without user consent or notification
file_indicators: Hardcoded wallet addresses (e.g., 0x658729879fca881d9526480b82ae00efc54b5c2d) present in JavaScript files
Unusual or unauthorized changes to main entry files (index.js) in package versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, and 1.1.7
References to rogue WalletConnect project IDs in configuration objects
network_indicators: Connections to WalletConnect projects not associated with Ledger or official partners
Outgoing transactions on blockchain networks directed to known attacker-controlled wallet addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installations of @ledgerhq/connect-kit versions 1.1.5, 1.1.6, and 1.1.7. Analyze JavaScript bundles for hardcoded wallet addresses and non-official WalletConnect project IDs. Flag any code that intercepts and modifies transaction parameters, especially if the recipient address is replaced without user interaction. Monitor outgoing blockchain transactions for known attacker wallet addresses (e.g., 0x658729879fca881d9526480b82ae00efc54b5c2d).
